headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP overlap: Goose can write broadly while TREK handles secrets and collaborative state, creating medium-to-high leakage, conflict, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Goose can use MCP, read/write the filesystem, and run shell commands; TREK also uses MCP and real-time collaboration. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content or shared files are treated as trusted input. The pair is not documented directly, so uncertainty pushes upward from low.
conditions: IF Goose ingests TREK-produced files or MCP messages as instructions, injected content can steer tool use.
IF both agents share a filesystem or message bus without provenance tags, prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from shared files.
Add provenance labels to MCP/file inputs.
Separate workspaces per agent.
Require human review before executing TREK-originated commands.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Goose has broad filesystem read/write and handles model-provider and extension tokens; TREK touches travel plans, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets. If they share files or a workspace, Goose can read sensitive TREK data and its broad network egress can exfiltrate it. The interaction is not directly documented, so this is inferred but still dangerous by default.
conditions: IF Goose and TREK share any writable workspace, Goose can read TREK secrets or documents.
IF Goose forwards retrieved context to configured model providers, sensitive TREK data can leave the host.
mitigations: Keep separate directories and mounts.
Remove secrets from shared folders.
Restrict Goose network egress to approved endpoints.
Rotate any TREK secrets exposed in shared files.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and DLP controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Goose can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; TREK is collaborative and uses files plus real-time sessions. If both operate on the same repo or data directory, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite each other, especially without locking. Because shared-state via filesystem is explicit for Goose, the conflict pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
IF TREK and Goose edit shared collaborative records without locks, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Assign disjoint write paths.
Pause one agent during git operations.
Use file locks for shared artifacts.
Commit through a single designated writer.
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Goose can generate code, shell actions, and MCP-driven outputs; TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in and can act on documents, reservations, and user accounts. If TREK consumes Goose output as authoritative, a mistaken plan or command can cascade into incorrect travel actions. The pairwise pathway is inferred rather than directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK treats Goose output as authoritative without verification, downstream actions can be wrong.
IF Goose emits malformed commands or facts into TREK workflows, TREK may propagate them to reservations or user-facing records.
mitigations: Require verification before TREK acts on Goose output.
Add schema checks for Goose-produced artifacts.
Log and review high-impact actions.
Limit Goose output to drafts only.
requires-engineering: implement confidence gating and human approval for bookings or account changes.

E_compliance.rationale: Goose is on-machine and handles model-provider keys and extension tokens, while TREK is self-hosted and handles OIDC secrets, API keys, MFA secrets, and user-account data. If Goose processes TREK data under a different residency or retention regime, compliance gaps can arise. The profiles do not specify exact jurisdictions, so this is a conservative medium finding rather than high.
conditions: IF TREK data includes regulated personal data and Goose sends it to external model providers, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF the two agents retain logs under different policies, deletion or export requests may fail end-to-end.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Goose.
Align retention settings across both systems.
Document data-flow boundaries.
Review vendor DPAs and hosting regions.
requires-engineering: implement subject-rights and residency controls end-to-end.
